chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ أَخَاهُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ

translations.en: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them.

chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي السَّفِينَةِ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَضَعَ الْحَصِيرَ عَلَى الْمَتَاعِ أَوِ الْقَتِّ وَالتِّبْنِ وَالْحِنْطَةِ وَالشَّعِيرِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ

translations.en: About a man who is on a ship: is it permissible for him to place a mat over goods, or al-qatt, straw, wheat, barley, and other than that, then perform salat (prayer) on it?
So he said: "There is no harm."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning performing salat (prayer) on a ship when ordinary conditions on land are unavailable. It indicates that placing a mat over cargo or similar materials and praying on it is permissible, showing practical ease in worship during travel.
en.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on a mat placed over goods or grain while on a ship?

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the ship; the setting in which the ruling applies
key_terms.الْحَصِيرَ: the mat placed as a surface for prayer
key_terms.الْمَتَاعِ: goods or belongings carried on the ship
key_terms.الْحِنْطَةِ: wheat; one of the materials mentioned beneath the mat
key_terms.الشَّعِيرِ: barley; another material mentioned beneath the mat
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; a formula indicating permissibility
